subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group isolation be solved by sender/topic-scoped sessions plus memory namespaces, automatic per-user group subagents, or an external/plugin experiment before adding SDK/core contracts?
rationale: The request crosses product, security, plugin API, memory isolation, admin authority, lifecycle, cost, and message-routing boundaries that source inspection cannot safely choose automatically.

options.title: Design The Feishu Isolation Seam First
options.body: Use current sender/topic session and subagent binding primitives as inputs, define memory/config/lifecycle/security boundaries, and only then implement the approved seam.

options.title: Prototype In The Feishu Plugin
options.body: Validate routing, cleanup, quotas, shared/private memory, and admin controls in the Feishu plugin before promoting any SDK or core contract.

options.title: Defer Heavy Group Subagents
options.body: Do not add automatic group subagent orchestration now; keep narrower session-routing, threading, and skill-preference issues open for targeted work.

recommendation.title: Design The Feishu Isolation Seam First
recommendation.body: Use current sender/topic session and subagent binding primitives as inputs, define memory/config/lifecycle/security boundaries, and only then implement the approved seam.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the documented community-maintained owner signal for the Feishu plugin and are the strongest follow-up owner in the issue timeline.
